workflow.selector_prompt: Select the single Quecto repository workflow template, 'feature', before checking steps.

templates.label: Feature
templates.description: New capability with local hook verification, BDD/TDD, code review, then hand off the PR for human review (no auto-merge).
templates.when_to_use: Use for all Quecto development work in this repository.
templates.shared_guidance: Shared sub-agent review mechanic (used by both the `bdd_review` and `reviewers` steps): launch each reviewer with `spawn`, binding it to its OWN dedicated review workflow via `workflow_spec`/`template` (never this feature workflow). Spawned reviewers are auto-awaited — you automatically receive a one-line completion note for each at your next idle turn, so an explicit `agent_cmd` `command: 'await'` is optional; use it only if you must block before doing anything else. When you need a reviewer's findings to proceed, read them with `get_messages` (after its completion note, or after an explicit await). Record each spawned sub-agent id for the cleanup step. For PR reviewers, reviewers must not be dispatched before a PR exists; the reviewer task must receive a PR number, not a raw diff.

steps.label: Install/check local quality hooks
steps.guidance: Run `scripts/install-hooks.sh`, then verify pre-commit, pre-push, and the git --no-verify wrapper are installed/active before editing code. See `docs/agent-dev-quickstart.md` for repo orientation, crate names, targeted tests, gh recipes, hooks, coverage, and gotchas. Hook summary: `git commit` pre-commit does NOT run unit/BDD tests; it runs quality/BDD-quality gates, `cargo fmt --check`, strict clippy, and fast guard tests. `git push` pre-push runs the full new+old suite and can take minutes. Never bypass hooks with --no-verify. Done when all three hooks are installed and active.

steps.label: Update Scenarios / Add new features
steps.guidance: First read the issue and comments with `gh issue view <N> --json title,body,comments`. Update BDD feature files and task-facing scenarios first, and identify explicit, checkable acceptance criteria for the change. See `docs/agent-dev-quickstart.md` for repo orientation, crate names, targeted tests, gh recipes, hooks, coverage, and gotchas. BDD selection is by tag + sharding (no scenario-name filter unless implemented). The acceptance criteria identified here are the SAME checklist the later `conformance` step verifies against branch code, so make them concrete and testable. Done when the scenarios are updated and the acceptance criteria are written down.

steps.label: Write/update unit tests (run a quick smoke check; full suite runs on push)
steps.guidance: Write or update unit tests for the change. Use the crate names from `docs/agent-dev-quickstart.md`: kernel `cargo test -p quecto --lib <name_substring>`; TUI `cargo test -p quecto-tui --lib <name_substring>`; never `-p quecto-agentic-harness`. Plain lib tests need no `--features`; render-harness-driven TUI BDD uses the integration `bdd` target with `--features test-harness`. Run a quick targeted smoke check to confirm tests compile; the full suite and coverage run on push. Done when the new/modified tests compile and target the new behaviour.

steps.label: Ensure new/modified tests FAIL (RED) — quick targeted run only, not full suite
steps.guidance: Run a quick targeted check: only the new/modified targeted test to confirm it fails before implementation: `cargo test -p quecto --lib <name_substring>` or `cargo test -p quecto-tui --lib <name_substring>` as documented in `docs/agent-dev-quickstart.md`. Do not run the whole suite here. Done when the new tests fail for the expected reason. If it fails to fail — i.e. a new test passes before implementation — it is not exercising the new behaviour, so fix the test.

steps.label: Despatch BDD sub-agent to review BDD feature, step tests and unit tests
steps.guidance: Using the feature template's shared sub-agent review mechanic (the `shared_guidance` field), run an independent BDD/test-quality review (its OWN review workflow, not this one). Give the reviewer the issue details, the changed BDD feature files, step tests and unit tests, and its single dimension 'BDD/test quality': verify scenarios follow BDD best practice (clear Given-When-Then, explicit and testable acceptance criteria, one logical scenario per feature, no implementation detail in steps, appropriate step abstraction and reuse), and that unit tests are behavioural, well-named, focused and assert the right things. The reviewer must be skeptical (report only real issues), must NOT modify code, and must return file:line findings with severity, the problem and a concrete fix. Fix any valid concerns before the GREEN step. Done when the BDD review has returned and valid concerns are fixed.

steps.label: Implement code (GREEN)
steps.guidance: Write the code needed to satisfy the failing tests. Do NOT worry about the size of a change — implement it in full. Done when the previously-failing tests pass.

steps.label: Refactor
steps.guidance: Tidy only what this change touches — naming, duplication, clarity. Keep it minimal; no speculative abstraction or unrelated cleanup.

steps.label: Ensure tests still pass
steps.guidance: Run `cargo fmt` and targeted strict clippy locally first (for kernel: `cargo clippy -p quecto --all-targets -- -D warnings`; see `docs/agent-dev-quickstart.md` for coverage env vars and TUI/test-support footguns), then re-run only the targeted tests and confirm GREEN. Do not manually re-run the whole suite before commit; push/pre-push is the full-suite mechanism. Respect the 750-line file cap and strict clippy before pushing. Done when targeted tests pass and fmt/clippy are clean. If it fails, fix the code — never silence clippy — before pushing.

steps.label: Commit
steps.guidance: If on the default branch, create a feature branch first. Stage only the files you changed (`git add <paths>`); never `git add -A` or `git add .` — that sweeps untracked tooling (e.g. `.claude/`) and build artifacts (e.g. `target*/`) into the commit. See `docs/agent-dev-quickstart.md` for repo orientation, crate names, targeted tests, gh recipes, hooks, coverage, and gotchas. Remember `git commit` runs the pre-commit structure/lint/fast-guard gate, not unit/BDD feature tests. Write a clear, descriptive commit message and include any commit trailers your harness requires. Done when only the intended files are staged and committed on a feature branch.

steps.label: Push (pre-push hook will run tests and linting)
steps.guidance: Push triggers the full local gate (or validate without pushing via `scripts/pre-push.sh`; see `docs/agent-dev-quickstart.md`): fmt, strict clippy, unit/integration/architecture/contracts/repo_docs/workflow_config, the 24-shard non-real BDD suite, region coverage at or above 87% for quecto and quecto-tui, machete and deny. The zero-cost mocked `@mock-llm` e2e lane runs by default; the live LLM suite (tagged `@manual-real-llm`) is opt-in via `QUECTO_RUN_REAL_LLM=1`. The `find.feature` "Nested .gitignore … in git repo" scenario is load-flaky under the parallel shard wave — re-run the shard before treating it as a real failure (it passes in isolation). Push may take minutes and is not hung. Fix every failure; never use --no-verify. Done when the full gate is green. If it fails only on the flaky find.feature scenario, re-run the shard; otherwise fix the failure.

steps.label: Create PR
steps.guidance: Open the PR against the default branch with gh, with a clear title and a body that summarizes the change. The required CI checks are "Unit Tests" and "Mock LLM E2E Tests". Do not claim to co-author it. Done when the PR is open and the required checks are running.

steps.label: Despatch sub agents in parallel as reviewers (Architecture, Security and Performance)
steps.guidance: Precondition: reviewers MUST NOT be dispatched before a PR exists; if no PR number is available, stop and complete the Create PR step first. Use `gh pr view <PR> --json id,headRefOid,state,mergeStateStatus`, `gh pr diff <PR>`, and the `addPullRequestReview` event COMMENT snippet in `docs/agent-dev-quickstart.md`. Using the feature template shared sub-agent review mechanic, dispatch reviewers in a SINGLE parallel batch, each bound to its OWN `review-pr` workflow and given only the PR number, head commit SHA, single review dimension and file scope. Explicitly forbid passing a raw diff: reviewers must fetch the diff themselves from the PR number. Dimensions (ALWAYS dispatch all of these as the default set): Architecture, Security, Performance, Correctness (logic, edge cases, silent-wrong-answer footguns), Conformance-to-AC (re-read the issue acceptance criteria and check each is actually met, including documentation and protocol updates), and Test-quality. Scale further for large diffs. Every reviewer MUST post findings as INLINE review comments on the PR via GitHub GraphQL (`addPullRequestReview` event COMMENT with comments array, or equivalent). If a line anchor is rejected, fall back to a review comment that still cites file:line. Each finding states file:line, severity, the problem and a concrete fix. CRITICAL: each reviewer MUST SUBMIT the review — never leave it PENDING; verify submittedAt != null. Done when every reviewer has posted inline findings and a submitted (non-PENDING) review on the PR.

steps.label: Fix all valid review concerns
steps.guidance: Triage each inline finding — confirm it is genuinely valid before changing anything (reviewers can be wrong). Fix forward in the same branch. Track which findings you accept versus decline; you reply to all of them in the resolve step. Done when every valid finding has a fix in the branch.

steps.label: Push changes to remote
steps.guidance: Push the fixes; the full pre-push gate runs again. Wait for it to pass before resolving threads.

steps.label: Reply to the reviewers comments on the PR and mark resolved (use graphql)
steps.guidance: Reply to EVERY review comment on the PR — for accepted findings note the fix and commit, for declined ones explain why — then resolve each thread with the GraphQL resolveReviewThread mutation. Thread ids come from the PR reviewThreads connection. Done when every review thread is resolved.

steps.label: Verify the PR meets every issue acceptance criterion
steps.guidance: Read the original issue and comments with `gh issue view <N> --json title,body,comments`, then systematically verify EACH acceptance criterion from the issue (the same checklist captured in `scenarios`) against the ACTUAL branch code, citing file:line evidence. Use `docs/agent-dev-quickstart.md` for repo orientation and gh commands. A criterion counts as met only when the evidence is in the code — never on the PR description claims; be skeptical. Output a per-criterion table marking each met/partial/unmet with evidence, then a final verdict line: `CONFORMANCE: PASS` only if every criterion is fully met, otherwise `CONFORMANCE: FAIL` listing gaps. On `CONFORMANCE: FAIL`, fix the gaps and re-verify before reporting — do NOT merge on a FAIL. Done when the verdict is `CONFORMANCE: PASS` with file:line evidence for every criterion.

steps.label: Confirm the pre-push gate passed and report the PR (do NOT merge)
steps.guidance: Confirm the latest push's pre-push gate passed in full (coverage threshold, machete, deny, and the mocked `@mock-llm` e2e lane that runs by default; the live LLM suite is opt-in via `QUECTO_RUN_REAL_LLM=1`) and the required CI checks "Unit Tests" and "Mock LLM E2E Tests" are green. Also confirm the reviewers actually POSTED inline findings on the PR (not just a returned summary) and that all review threads are resolved. The `find.feature` "Nested .gitignore … in git repo" scenario is load-flaky — re-run the shard before treating it as a real failure. Do NOT run gh pr merge or git merge, and do NOT set auto-merge: this workflow never merges. Report the PR number and a short summary, then STOP — the master agent and a human own merging. For the PR to be mergeable the required "Unit Tests" and "Mock LLM E2E Tests" checks must be green and the verdict must be CONFORMANCE: PASS; if any review, fix, or conformance step ERRORED or did not actually run, or the push bypassed the local gate with --no-verify, report that too. Done when the gate and required checks are green, inline findings were posted, all threads are resolved, and the PR is reported as ready for review (NOT merged).

steps.label: Clean up sub agents
steps.guidance: Reviewers that have already reported completion (you received their one-line completion notes) have exited and need no cleanup. Check `get_subagents` for any sub agent still running, and only then terminate the stragglers (use agent_cmd to abort, or kill each) so no orphaned sub agents remain.

guards.message: Complete hook setup and RED/GREEN work before committing.

This workflow does NOT merge — report the PR for review and stop. Before reporting, complete code review, pass the conformance gate (CONFORMANCE: PASS), and verify the pre-push gate genuinely passed (not bypassed with --no-verify). Never run gh pr merge / git merge or set auto-merge; report the PR as ready for review instead.
